basic_details.job_title: CSIR-NBRI Recruitment 2026 – Walkin for 3 Project Assistant, Senior-PAT and More Posts
basic_details.short_information: CSIR-National Botanical Research Institute (CSIR-NBRI), Lucknow will hold a walk-in interview on 04 December 2026 for three purely temporary posts under sponsored projects. Reporting time is 10:00 AM at K. N. Kaul Block, CSIR-NBRI, Rana Pratap Marg, Lucknow, and candidates will not be permitted to enter the venue after 11:00 AM. The posts are Senior-PAT, Project Assistant-II and Junior Research Assistant, one position each, with pay from Rs. 20,000 to Rs. 42,000 plus HRA as sanctioned in the projects (Advertisement No. 12/Project/2026).

content_sections.heading: What to Bring
content_sections.text: One latest photograph. Original documents, with self-attested copies of certificates of examinations passed (starting from matriculation). A certificate indicating date of birth. Experience certificate, etc. The application form: it will be provided at the venue on the interview day, or can be downloaded in advance from www.nbri.res.in . Tentative mark sheets/certificates and "result awaited" documents will not be considered.

content_sections.heading: What Happens on the Day
content_sections.text: All eligible candidates are requested to be present at the venue one hour before the scheduled time for document verification. Selection is through interview. If a large number of candidates turn up, a screening test of multiple-choice objective questions may be held to shortlist candidates for the interview. The Selection Committee interviews the shortlisted candidates. A panel of recommended candidates is formed on the basis of interview performance and used as and when the requirement arises in the projects in the relevant field/area. Candidates may interact with the committee in Hindi or English. If many candidates turn up, interviews may continue till late in the evening or the next day, so candidates are asked to plan their travel accordingly.

faq.question: Q1. What are the date, time and venue of the CSIR-NBRI walk-in interview?
faq.answer: The walk-in interview is on 04.12.2026 for both Area-I and Area-II, with reporting at 10:00 AM at K. N. Kaul Block, CSIR-NBRI, Rana Pratap Marg, Lucknow. Entry is not permitted after 11:00 AM.

faq.question: Q2. How many vacancies are there in CSIR-NBRI Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: There are three positions: one each for Senior-PAT, Project Assistant-II and Junior Research Assistant. The notice says the number of positions may vary at the time of selection.

faq.question: Q3. What is the qualification for Senior-PAT?
faq.answer: Masters/Integrated Masters in Natural, Agricultural, Pharmaceutical, Environmental, Plant or Life Sciences or Biotechnology with 03 years' relevant experience, or a Doctoral Degree in the same subjects from a recognized University or equivalent.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit for the posts?
faq.answer: Senior-PAT is 40 years and Project Assistant-II is 35 years. Junior Research Assistant is a maximum of 28 years as on 01.04.2026. SC/ST/PwBD/Women get 05 years' relaxation and OBC 03 years, except for Junior Research Assistant, where CSTUP guidelines apply.

faq.question: Q5. What is the pay for each post?
faq.answer: Senior-PAT gets Rs. 42,000 plus HRA and Project Assistant-II gets Rs. 20,000 plus HRA, with a 15% increment after 03 years of experience in the same project. Junior Research Assistant gets Rs. 25,000 per month for two years and Rs. 28,000 for the third year.

faq.question: Q6. Is HRA paid on top of the pay?
faq.answer: HRA is shown with the pay of Senior-PAT and Project Assistant-II, and the notice says HRA will be admissible as per sanction in the projects. No HRA is printed against the Junior Research Assistant pay. No TA/DA is admissible.

faq.question: Q7. Which documents should I bring?
faq.answer: Bring one latest photograph, original documents with self-attested copies of certificates of examinations passed from matriculation, a date of birth certificate and an experience certificate. Tentative mark sheets and "result awaited" documents are not accepted.

faq.question: Q8. How are candidates selected?
faq.answer: Selection is through interview before the Selection Committee. If many candidates turn up, a multiple-choice screening test may be held first to shortlist candidates for the interview.

faq.question: Q9. Who can apply for the Junior Research Assistant post?
faq.answer: Only Indian citizens who are residents of Uttar Pradesh are eligible for this post. The qualification is an M.Sc. in Botany/Environmental Sciences/Microbiology or M.Sc. (Ag) in Horticulture, with 1st Class in B.Sc and M.Sc.

faq.question: Q10. Is this a permanent job?
faq.answer: No, the posts are described as purely temporary under sponsored projects. Appointment is co-terminus with the project, and total tenure of project staff in CSIR projects should not exceed 06 years, subject to the exception stated in the notice.
